Moshiach ben Yosef and Moshiach ben David
the twelve tribes and their paths
the six orders of Mishnah and the days of the week

title.en: Each tribe with its own judges

summary.en: The Rav brings the Chasam Sofer on 'shoftim veshotrim': each tribe has its own gate in the Beis Hamikdash, its own nusach and even its own halachos, so each needs its own judges. He contrasts the Avos, who each included all of Klal Yisrael, with the tribes, the branches that divide off from the trunk.

title.en: Yerushalayim, where the tribes go up

summary.en: The Rav explains that each month and each of the twelve weekday blessings corresponds to a tribe, while Shabbos and the festivals rise to the Avos. Yerushalayim is where the tribes go up beyond their division to the fiftieth gate, and so a matter 'too wondrous' for the tribal judges goes up to the Sanhedrin in the Beis Hamikdash.

title.en: Ben zekunim: five orders, not six

summary.en: The Rav brings the Baal HaTurim that 'ben zekunim' hints at the orders Yaakov taught Yosef, without Taharos, and the Chasam Sofer's explanation that Yosef therefore could not use the Divine Name against his brothers. He asks why Yaakov needed teachers when Avraham kept the whole Torah himself, and how Yaakov could tell from grain in Egypt that Yosef was alive.

title.en: Yosef raised to the seven shepherds

summary.en: The Rav explains that the seven shepherds are above the division of the tribes, like Shabbos, and that in the future the river will split into seven streams rather than twelve. Yosef was raised above his brothers to be one of the shepherds, 'noheg katzon Yosef', with Ephraim and Menashe filling his place among the tribes; the brothers did not understand this.

title.en: The days of the week and the orders of Mishnah

summary.en: From the Chok LeYisrael's daily order of learning, the Rav matches the days of the week to the seven shepherds and the orders of Mishnah. Avraham's chesed accompanies all the days, so he kept the whole Torah himself; Yitzchak is Moed, Yaakov Nashim, and Yosef, Friday, is Taharos, which he mastered himself, which is why Yaakov loved him as 'ben zekunim'.

title.en: Taharos gives the fruit its taste and smell

summary.en: The Rav completes the orders: Moshe is Nezikin, Aharon Kodashim, and David the level of sod and Shabbos. He brings the Gemara at the end of Sotah that tahara gives fruit its taste and smell, and explains that Yaakov smelled this in the grain Yosef had handled in Egypt, and so knew Yosef was alive.

title.en: Eretz Yisrael, the chosen place, and erev Shabbos

summary.en: The Rav brings the Chasam Sofer that Moshe mentions Eretz Yisrael constantly in Devarim because mentioning it, like mentioning a tzaddik's name, brings yiras shamayim. Parshas Re'eh, read when Elul is blessed, repeats 'the place Hashem will choose'; there are two mikdashim, Yosef's and David's, and Yosef's, Friday, prepares for David's as erev Shabbos prepares for Shabbos.

title.en: Elul is Yosef's month, Tishrei is David's

summary.en: The Rav explains that Shechem is Yosef's own place, and 'ad mekom Shechem' equals Taharos in gematria. Following the Arizal's order of months and middos, Elul, the sixth month, belongs to Yosef by the seven shepherds though not by the tribal banners, and Tishrei to David: Elul is Moshiach ben Yosef preparing for Moshiach ben David, and the shofar of Elul and of Tishrei are the two shofros of Moshiach.

title.en: The captives who trembled at the Elul shofar

summary.en: The Rav tells a story handed down from Rebbe Reb Elimelech about a woman whose husband had disappeared and who was sent with a letter to a house in the forest, where he was held by forces of impurity. The husband later related that when Jews blew the shofar in Elul his captors trembled in terror; the Rav explains that the Elul shofar awakens the light of Moshiach ben Yosef that prepares for Tishrei.

title.en: Shiloh without walls: the King in the field

summary.en: The Rav explains that Re'eh moves from the festivals of the Avos to 'the place Hashem will choose', and that Elul, Yosef's mikdash in Shiloh, has an advantage over Tishrei: in Shiloh kodashim were eaten wherever it could be seen, with no wall. He brings the Baal HaTanya's parable of the king in the field whom anyone may approach, and ties the open sanctity of Shiloh to Yosef's guarding of his eyes.

title.en: Yosef's trials and the fragrance of Elul

summary.en: The Rav describes Yosef's trials as a boy of seventeen cut off from home, through which he merited tahara. He brings the Gemara that 'the dudaim gave off fragrance' refers to young men who never tasted sin, ties reiach to Yosef and to Elul ('ani ledodi'), and says the trials grow each year and teshuvah turns sin to merit. He also brings that the fragrance of the ketores was still smelled long after the destruction.

title.en: Teshuvah in the air and tzedakah of yesod

summary.en: The Rav explains that the teshuvah of the generation of the wilderness during Moshe's forty days remains in the air of Elul, and that Moshe left no soul 'at the end of the heavens' without the ability to return. Yosef's midah of yesod is tzedakah, which is chesed and draws down good beyond what one earns; 'ish lere'ehu umatanos la'evyonim' spells Elul, the time of teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah.

title.en: The treasuries are open: using Elul

summary.en: The Rav brings 'adam bikar velo yavin': one placed before open treasuries who takes nothing is like an animal, and so are the days of Elul, days of will when the treasuries are open. He calls to use them to prepare for Rosh Hashanah, explains 'zochreini... bechirecha' as Hashem remembering His chosen people, and, following the way of tzaddikim, gives hints for the coming year.

title.en: The shofar, the fiftieth gate and trembling

summary.en: The Rav explains that the shofar is the level of the fiftieth gate and of yovel, the freedom and return of the future. He repeats that the forces of impurity tremble at the Jewish shofar and asks how much more a Jew should tremble, laments that today minds are blocked, and says one must learn in seforim what Elul is. He closes with a blessing that the month bring teshuvah sheleimah and the redemption.

catalogTitle: “...אמר אל הכהנים בני אהרן ואמרת...” As we Purify Ourselves Hashem Purifies us

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains Sefirah and the Omer of Parshas Emor as Hashem's purifying and lifting up of every fallen Jew, from the lowest to the forgotten, with Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, Purim and even Tisha B'Av as part of that uplifting.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the Midrash linking 'Emor... v'amarta' to 'Imros Hashem amaros tehoros', words refined seven times seven, and explains that Sefirah is like pure water sprinkled from above: we count, and Hashem cleanses us, coming toward us like a chassan toward his kallah on Lag Baomer. The days are vessels of the middos, and Hashem counts with us. He then reads the Omer's tenufah: Yidden are Hashem's crop, with holy grain for the kohen and leket, shikchah and peah for the poor and forgotten. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai reveals the good in every Jew, as at Meron. The Omer of barley, like the sotah's offering, proves the Yidden stayed pure in Mitzrayim; lifting the Omer means lifting the fallen, as Rashbi purified Tiveria. Tisha B'Av, Purim and Lag Baomer belong to the fallen, and the parsha of the son of Shlomis bas Divri and the end of Eicha promise that even the lowest will be raised.

en: Sefirah is like pure water sprinkled from above: Yidden only count, and Hashem Himself purifies them over the seven times seven days.
Yidden are Hashem's crop, and just as a field has holy grain for the kohen and grain at the edges for the poor, Klal Yisrael has its fallen and forgotten Jews who belong to Hashem as well.
Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai reveals the good part in every Jew, which is why every kind of Jew comes to Meron and why his day is Hod shebeHod, the lowest level of Sefirah.
The command to lift the Omer means that the kohen, the tzaddik, must lift up the Yidden who fell after the first day of Pesach, and Sefirah raises them back to where they belong.

Tisha B'Av, Purim and Lag Baomer are the festivals of the fallen, and the parsha of the son of the Israelite woman is placed in Emor as the Tisha B'Av, promising that even the lowest soul will be purified.

candidateTopics: purity of Klal Yisrael in Mitzrayim

title.en: Pure words and water from above

summary.en: The Rav opens with the Midrash on 'Emor... v'amarta' and 'Imros Hashem amaros tehoros', refined seven times seven, and explains that Sefirah is like water sprinkled from above rather than a mikveh one goes down into. On Hod shebeHod, Hashem comes out toward Klal Yisrael like a chassan toward his kallah.

title.en: Days as vessels of the middos

summary.en: The Rav explains that each day is a receptacle of one of the middos, bringing the Zohar on 'six days' and the Ushpizin, with Avraham's chesed accompanying every day. Counting shows longing, and Hashem also counts toward us, day after day like a fountain of pure water.

title.en: Hashem's field and its grain

summary.en: The Rav asks why the pasuk stresses lifting the Omer and explains that Yidden are Hashem's crop with many levels. He brings the Gemara on the measures of terumah, explains that in Temple times one could see how much holy grain grew in each field, and that peah, leket and shikchah belong to the poor, who are on the ground and forgotten.

title.en: Rabbi Shimon lifts every Jew

summary.en: The Rav brings the saying that whoever has emunah in Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai has strength from him, and that even the lowest Jew draws from him, as seen at Meron. Rashbi reveals the good part in every Jew, which is why his day is Hod shebeHod; he prepares Klal Yisrael as a kallah for Shavuos, when Megillas Rus is read about the lost soul who gathered leket and shikchah.

title.en: The Omer of barley and the fallen

summary.en: The Rav asks why the pesukim of leket and peah appear between Shavuos and Rosh Hashanah, and brings that the Omer, like the sotah's offering, is of barley, proving that the Yidden remained pure in Mitzrayim apart from one woman. He describes the poor in knowledge, the fallen and forgotten at the edge of Klal Yisrael's field, and the souls of the fallen Sukkas David.

title.en: Lifting the Omer, lifting the Yidden

summary.en: The Rav explains that on the first night of Pesach Hashem lifted the Yidden up through the 49 levels, and on the second day they fell back so they could climb on their own through Sefirah. 'Vehenif es ha'Omer' is Hashem's command to the kohen, the tzaddik, to lift up the fallen, and on Shavuos the two loaves are chametz because the chametz has been uplifted.

title.en: Rashbi, the purifier of Tiveria

summary.en: The Rav brings the Gemara that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai purified Tiveria of its lost graves and that its 'empty' Jews were uplifted by him, and the Zohar that he passed away on Lag Baomer while saying the word 'chaim'. He connects the sotah who is found pure and blessed to Rashbi's purifying, and to Rabbi Akiva's 'ashreichem Yisrael' sung on Lag Baomer.

title.en: Tisha B'Av, Purim and Lag Baomer

summary.en: The Rav compares the moadim to levels of tzaddikim, brings the Rokeach that all the festivals, including Chanukah and Purim, are hinted in Emor, and asks where Tisha B'Av is. He explains that Tisha B'Av is the moed of those who ruined themselves and will be rebuilt, and that Purim and Lag Baomer, which fall on the same weekday, are for the lowest Jews who are lifted up.

title.en: Shlomis bas Divri and her son

summary.en: The Rav explains why the parsha of the son of the Israelite woman follows the festivals: his mother, Shlomis bas Divri of the tribe of Dan, was the one Jewish soul who fell in Mitzrayim, through being overly familiar with everyone. She is the Tisha B'Av, her name alludes to teshuvah, and like the sotah's barley offering, the Omer and Sefirah will purify even her.

title.en: Double purification and 'Hashiveinu'

summary.en: The Rav explains that the Omer, though a sheep, has a double measure of flour because of a double purification: the Yidden count and Hashem counts. He closes with the last pesukim of Eichah, where the most forgotten Jews refuse to accept rejection and cry 'Hashiveinu', and with the blessing of the sotah and the coming of Yovel in Behar.

catalogTitle: אלול ותשרי - בזמן' כנגד ירשלים והר המוריה - במקום

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that just as the place of the Beis HaMikdash is the hidden starting point of creation in space and must be sought out, Rosh Hashanah is that point in time, and the forty days from Rosh Chodesh Elul are the climb up the mountain to reach it.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the parsha of the zaken mamre and asks why the Torah, which marks the location of Gerizim and Eival so precisely, never says where the Beis HaMikdash is, only 'seek out His dwelling'. He explains that the even shesiyah is the point from which the world was founded, the top of the globe and the root of creation. Following Sefer Yetzirah's world, year and soul, Rosh Hashanah is that point in time and Adam HaRishon, then Dovid HaMelech, in the soul; the forty days from Rosh Chodesh Elul are the formation of the year. The middle verse of Sefer Devarim is the verse about the Sanhedrin's place. Because the root is hidden, it must be searched for, as Dovid and Shmuel searched and erred before finding the place and the king. Elul is the climb up the mountain without sleeping, toward the kingship of Rosh Hashanah.

en: The Torah describes the location of Gerizim and Eival precisely but does not say where the Beis HaMikdash is, because that place must be sought out ('l'shichno sidreshu').
The even shesiyah is the point from which creation began and spread outward, and therefore it is the highest place, the top of the globe.
Following world, year and soul, Rosh Hashanah is the Beis HaMikdash of time, and the forty days from Rosh Chodesh Elul to Yom Kippur are the formation of the year.
The Sanhedrin, the root of the Torah's authority, sits in the place of the root of the world, and the middle verse of Sefer Devarim is the verse about that place.
Because the root point is hidden, Rosh Hashanah, like the place of the Mikdash and like Dovid himself, must be searched for with effort, and Elul is the time of that search.
Rosh Hashanah is the day of kingship, and the Yamim Nora'im are days of the Beis HaMikdash, as in 'how awesome is this place'.

candidateTopics: Rosh Hashanah as the head of the year

title.en: Why the Torah hides the Mikdash's place

summary.en: The Rav opens with the zaken mamre and the authority of the Sanhedrin, and asks why the Torah describes the location of Gerizim and Eival exactly but never says where the Beis HaMikdash is. He brings 'l'shichno sidreshu', Dovid HaMelech's oath not to sleep until he found the place, and the Ramban.

title.en: The even shesiyah, root and peak of the world

summary.en: The Rav explains that the world was founded from the even shesiyah and grew outward into Yerushalayim, Eretz Yisrael and the other lands. He answers how Yerushalayim can be the highest place with the image of a globe whose top is the point where it was formed, and suggests that 'har' is linked to 'herayon', conception.

title.en: World, year and soul: forty days of Elul

summary.en: Bringing Sefer Yetzirah's world, year and soul, the Rav says each mirrors the others. As a child is formed in forty days, the year is formed in the forty days from Rosh Chodesh Elul to Yom Kippur, and he cites that Rosh Hashanah equals Beis HaMikdash in gematria.

title.en: Rosh Hashanah, the even shesiyah of time

summary.en: The Rav explains that Hashem is 'found' in the days from Rosh Hashanah to Yom Kippur because He is then creating the year, and moving away from that point, like galus from Yerushalayim, is distance. Rosh Hashanah includes the whole year as the head includes the body, and the forty days are the time when tefillah can still shape the year.

title.en: From Rosh Chodesh Elul: climbing the mountain

summary.en: The Rav says that as Moshe Rabbeinu went up the mountain on Rosh Chodesh Elul, every Jew must start climbing the mountain of Hashem in time, since the place is in ruins but time is not. Tzaddikim reach the top in thirty days, others in forty, and 'who shall ascend the mountain of Hashem' is answered by 'the generation of those who seek Him'.

title.en: Adam HaRishon and the seed that holds the tree

summary.en: In the soul, the Rav says, Adam HaRishon includes all souls and is the even shesiyah of the soul, created on Rosh Hashanah. With the image of an apple seed that holds a whole tree, he explains 'the little holding the much' and why at the Mikdash, the meeting point of Creator and creation, the rules of time and space did not apply.

title.en: The Avos as the mountains; Torah as the blueprint

summary.en: The Rav explains that the Avos are the 'mountains', the root of Klal Yisrael that includes the whole people, and therefore they were born in Tishrei, a time that includes all time. He then brings that Hashem looked into the Torah and created the world, like an architect with a blueprint, so everything in world, year and soul is found in the Torah.

title.en: The middle of Sefer Devarim and the Sanhedrin

summary.en: The Rav explains that Sefer Devarim, a repetition of the whole Torah, also contains the whole world, so its middle should correspond to the root place. After the dispute whether the world was created in Tishrei or Nissan and the two ways to find the Torah's middle, he says the middle of Devarim is the zaken mamre parsha: the Sanhedrin, root of the Torah, sits in the root of the world, and 'the place causes'.

title.en: A hidden place, a hidden day: Elul's search

summary.en: Citing the Masorah that 'min hamakom hahu' is the middle verse of Devarim, the Rav explains that the Mikdash is not a place of nature and is hidden, so it must be sought. Rosh Hashanah is also hidden ('bakeseh') and cannot be entered suddenly; Elul is the search, a time of not sleeping, as reflected in the custom of rising early for Selichos, and one must come clean of hands and pure of heart.

title.en: Dovid and Shmuel searching and erring

summary.en: The Rav brings that Adam HaRishon's soul came into Dovid HaMelech, who is the Rosh Hashanah of the soul. Dovid erred in thinking the Mikdash belonged on high Eitam until the Torah showed Har HaMoriah, and Shmuel HaNavi erred among Yishai's sons until the hidden Dovid was chosen; one must search and wander until finding the truth. The king, like Rosh Hashanah, is the source of blessing for the whole year.

title.en: Doeg's envy and finding the King

summary.en: The Rav asks why Doeg envied Dovid for finding the place of the Mikdash, since anyone can be mechadesh in Torah. He answers that each person's chiddush follows his root, and Dovid, whose root is the Mikdash, found it, which showed that he and not Shaul was the king. The place of the Mikdash is where Hashem's kingship is revealed, and so Rosh Hashanah is the day of kingship and the Yamim Nora'im are days of 'how awesome is this place'.

title.en: At the foot of the mountain: stay awake

summary.en: The Rav says that standing at Rosh Chodesh Elul one is at the foot of the mountain and must ask both to reach Rosh Hashanah and to stay there all year. The Mikdash is a place of wakefulness, as Yaakov said 'and I did not know', so one does not sleep on Rosh Hashanah; he brings the Rambam's call of the shofar to wake the sleepers, and closes with a brachah for a year of geulah.

catalogTitle: המתיקות של יראת הרוממות- בשמך יגילון כל היום- ר"ת בכיה (שייכות לפרשת וילך- הקהל)

oneLiner.en: Starting from the order of the mishnayos in Rosh Hashanah and the mitzvah of hakhel, the Rav explains that Rosh Hashanah is the king of the year, a foretaste of the Rosh Hashanah of Moshiach, whose fear of Hashem is sweet and whose weeping, as 'b'shimcha yegilun kol hayom' hints, is a weeping of joy.

abstract.en: The Rav asks why the Mishnah in Rosh Hashanah places the chapter on sanctifying the month before the laws of shofar. He turns to parshas Vayelech and hakhel: the children are brought so that those who bring them earn reward, as Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya expounded, and the Chasam Sofer explains that parents give up some of their own spiritual gain for their children, like Avraham as opposed to Chanoch. The king who reads at hakhel embodies malchus shamayim and is the channel of blessing; a leader may be chosen by Heaven or appointed by the people. Rosh Hashanah is the king of the year, so the nasi sets its date, as Rabbi Yehoshua submitted to Rabban Gamliel. Hakhel gathers souls, Rosh Hashanah gathers days; the shofar speaks beyond words and is the shofar of Moshiach, whose fear is a sweet fear. Finally, citing the Chasam Sofer's hint that 'b'shimcha yegilun' spells bechiyah, he explains the joyful weeping of a child returning to his Father, through Hoshea and Yirmiyahu, and urges preparation through Elul and through Shabbos.

en: Children are brought to hakhel even though they understand nothing, because what they absorb then stays with them for life, and the parents give up some of their own spiritual gain to give it to them.

The king embodies and includes the whole nation, is the garment of malchus shamayim in this world, and is the channel through which all blessing flows to the people; therefore there is a mitzvah to fear him.
Rosh Hashanah is the king and head of the whole year; therefore the nasi, the head of the people, determines when Rosh Hashanah falls.

A leader appointed by the people and one chosen by Heaven both bring down the same blessing, but the revealed kingship of a Heaven-chosen leader is far sweeter, and this is what is asked for on Rosh Hashanah.
Every Rosh Hashanah holds a taste of the Rosh Hashanah of Moshiach, and its fear of Hashem is a fear of His greatness that is a sweet pleasure, not a dread of punishment.
One weeps on Rosh Hashanah, but with a weeping of joy, as the Chasam Sofer hints in 'b'shimcha yegilun kol hayom': the tears of a child who returns to his Father, mixed with shame and with happiness.
This joyful weeping on Rosh Hashanah needs preparation through the weeping of Elul and Selichos.

candidateTopics: Rosh Hashanah as king of the year
weeping of joy on Rosh Hashanah

title.en: Why the chapter on the new month precedes shofar

summary.en: The Rav notes that Rebbi arranged every Mishnah precisely, and asks why, in Rosh Hashanah, the third chapter opens with laws of sanctifying the month before the laws of shofar begin, instead of giving the laws of Rosh Hashanah their own chapter.

title.en: Hakhel and why the small children come

summary.en: From parshas Vayelech the Rav describes Moshe finishing the Torah and the mitzvah of hakhel after shemitah, and asks why infants who understand nothing are brought; he brings the Yerushalmi about Rabbi Yehoshua's mother bringing him to the beis medrash, and the opposite case of Elisha ben Avuyah.

title.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya and giving up for one's children

summary.en: The Rav brings Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya's derashah that the children come to give reward to those who bring them, and the Chasam Sofer's explanation: the parents would hear better alone, yet they sacrifice their own spiritual gain for their children; this is the way of Avraham, who taught others, as opposed to Chanoch, and he adds Rabbi Yechezkel of Kuzmir's parable of candy sugar and ordinary sugar.

title.en: The king as the channel of blessing

summary.en: The Rav explains why the king reads at hakhel: he includes the whole nation, is the garment of Hashem's kingship in the world, and is the channel of all blessing, as Pharaoh understood about his dream; talmidei chachamim are such kings, and a leader may be chosen by Heaven for his merits, like Yosef, or appointed by the people for the sake of Heaven, and then Hashem gives him the power to bestow.

title.en: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua

summary.en: The Rav retells the Gemara at the end of the second chapter of Rosh Hashanah: Rabban Gamliel ordered Rabbi Yehoshua to come with his staff and money on the day that was Yom Kippur by his reckoning, Rabbi Yehoshua submitted, and Rabban Gamliel kissed him; the Gemara teaches that even the least of leaders, once appointed, is like the greatest.

title.en: Rosh Hashanah, the king of the year

summary.en: The Rav explains that one fears the king because he is the garment of malchus shamayim, and through him comes to fear of Heaven; just as the king heads the nation, Rosh Hashanah heads the year in the dimension of time, so it is a source of yiras shamayim for the whole year, and therefore the nasi is the one who determines Rosh Hashanah.

title.en: Two kinds of Rosh Hashanah, two kinds of leaders

summary.en: The Rav distinguishes a Rosh Hashanah fixed by beis din, even in error, from one fixed by Heaven when the court could not sanctify the month in time, and likewise a leader chosen by the people from one chosen by Heaven; the blessing is the same but the taste differs, and on Rosh Hashanah one asks for revealed kingship, 'he'aras panim', which answers why the chapter on sanctifying the month opens the laws of shofar.

title.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, a nasi chosen by Heaven

summary.en: The Rav explains that Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya was made nasi by Heaven, shown by the white beard that grew at eighteen, and so he was the one to expound hakhel: the Father turns His face to the child, the generation is not orphaned; he adds that the Rambam requires even great scholars to listen to the king, who is the messenger of Hashem.

title.en: Hakhel of souls, hakhel of days, and the wordless shofar

summary.en: The Rav explains that hakhel gathers all Jewish souls to the king while Rosh Hashanah gathers all the days of the year to their king; with the completed Sefer Torah, in which every soul has a letter, the king reads to all of Israel, and malchiyos verses need not say 'king'; the shofar speaks without words, in thoughts too high for speech, and the Jewish heart understands it.

title.en: The king of kings and the fear of Moshiach's shofar

summary.en: The Rav compares the children at hakhel to Jews hearing the shofar, then describes three levels of king, up to the soul of Adam, David and Moshiach, and the Rosh Hashanah of the redemption, 'v'nisgav Hashem levado'; the shofar casts fear, and at Moshiach's shofar the nations will hide from 'pachad Hashem umehadar geono', a fear of Hashem's greatness.

title.en: The sweet fear of Rosh Hashanah

summary.en: The Rav teaches that every Jewish king and every Rosh Hashanah is a foretaste of Moshiach; the prayer 'uv'chein tein pachdecha' asks for this fear, which a gentile cannot want but a Jew, tuned to Moshiach, longs for, since one who fears Hashem lacks nothing; like 'lefanav na'avod b'yirah vafachad' on Shabbos, this fear of the King is the greatest pleasure.

title.en: The shofar of Moshiach and the tekios of the Avos

summary.en: The Rav explains that Adam, created on Rosh Hashanah, is one soul with David and Moshiach, and teshuvah repairs Adam's sin; following the siddur of Rabbi Yaakov Emden the sounds correspond to the Avos and David, and the tekiah gedolah is the great shofar that will gather the exiles; at hakhel too trumpets were blown, and hakhel falls in the eighth year.

title.en: 'B'shimcha yegilun' spells bechiyah

summary.en: The Rav brings Nechemiah's words not to be sad on Rosh Hashanah and a parable of a prisoner who rejoices on the king's coronation day although it is his own day of judgment, against the Arizal's statement that one must weep on Rosh Hashanah; he resolves it with the Chasam Sofer, that 'b'shimcha yegilun kol hayom' is the roshei teivos of bechiyah: a weeping of joy.

title.en: Hoshea: a child cannot be exchanged

summary.en: The Rav explains that the weeping is that of a child returning to his Father, mixed with shame and joy, and reads the opening of Hoshea: Hashem told the prophet who suggested exchanging Israel to marry a harlot and then asked whether he could exchange his own children; the names Lo Ruchamah and Lo Ami are reversed, and Hashem loves Israel in every state.

title.en: Returning with tears to the Father

summary.en: From the end of Hoshea and Rashi the Rav explains that Israel will seek again malchus shamayim, the kingship of the house of David and the Beis Hamikdash, with a fear of Hashem's goodness; from the haftarah of the second day, 'bivchi yavo'u', he shows that the return from exile is with tears of a child coming back to his Father, the weeping of Rosh Hashanah.

title.en: Preparing the tears, and the Shabbos before Rosh Hashanah

summary.en: The Rav says one cannot suddenly weep tears of return without preparation; the tears of Elul and Selichos wash the face of the Shechinah, and only then can one hear the shofar of Moshiach. Since this Rosh Hashanah begins on Shabbos and the shofar is not blown, Shabbos must plead for us, so one must prepare for the last Shabbos of the year, and he brings Rabbi Shlomo of Karlin on one who has no longing for Shabbos.

catalogTitle: ר"ה יום כללי שמשפיע על כל השנה; הצלחה בר"ה ע"י עניוות ודביקות בצדיקים

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that Rosh Hashanah is the general root day from which the whole year is drawn, the 'Yerushalayim of time', and that its success comes through total self-nullification and binding oneself to the tzaddikim and all of Klal Yisrael.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with 'Atem nitzavim hayom', read before Rosh Hashanah, and explains that every day of the year hangs on Rosh Hashanah, the 'factory' where everything is made. He distinguishes the judgment of Rosh Hashanah, which allots the general flow of blessing for the year and sometimes for many years, from the daily judgment, which can only redirect within it, illustrating this with stories of the Ba'al Shem Tov and others. Sarah, Rachel and Chana were remembered on Rosh Hashanah itself because their remembrance concerned all of Klal Yisrael. Rosh Hashanah is the Yerushalayim of time, and so it is the day to pray for barren Yerushalayim and Eretz Yisrael, whose fate the nations cannot decide; Hashem laughs at their uproar. Finally he teaches that Rosh Hashanah should bring joyous fear of Heaven for the whole year, and that its success comes through humility and joining oneself to the tzaddikim and all of Klal Yisrael.

en: Every day of the year draws its character from Rosh Hashanah, which is the root of all the days.
On Rosh Hashanah the general flow of blessing is decided; the daily judgment can only redirect it within what was already allotted.
Sarah, Rachel and Chana were remembered on Rosh Hashanah itself because their remembrance was a general one that concerned all of Klal Yisrael.
Rosh Hashanah is to time what Yerushalayim is to place, and on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur the kingship comes to every Jew wherever he is.
Yerushalayim is like a barren woman, and Rosh Hashanah is the time to pray that she be remembered; her fate is not in the hands of the nations.
Rosh Hashanah is the source of fear of Heaven for the whole year, a fear that comes with joy in the King's coronation.
The success of Rosh Hashanah comes through being nothing before Hashem and through binding oneself to all the tzaddikim and all of Klal Yisrael.

candidateTopics: Rosh Hashanah as the root of the year
judgment on Rosh Hashanah and every day
Sarah, Rachel and Chana remembered on Rosh Hashanah
unity with Klal Yisrael and the tzaddikim

title.en: Every day hangs on Rosh Hashanah

summary.en: The Rav opens with 'Atem nitzavim hayom' and explains that 'hayom' means Rosh Hashanah, the root of every day of the year. He tells of Rabbi Pinchas of Koretz and the shtender, brings that Sarah, Rachel and Chana were remembered on Rosh Hashanah, and compares Rosh Hashanah to the factory where everything is made to order.

title.en: Judged on Rosh Hashanah and judged every day

summary.en: The Rav asks why Rosh Hashanah needs such effort if a person is judged every day, and answers that on Rosh Hashanah everything is judged both in detail and in general. He illustrates the detail with Rav Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld, who did not agree to a shidduch for a child he had not davened for on Rosh Hashanah, and the general with the years of plenty decided for Pharaoh.

title.en: Redirecting the year's blessing: two stories

summary.en: The Rav tells how the Ba'al Shem Tov could give a wealthy man a child only by turning his allotted wealth into children, leaving him poor, and a story of a chassid of Reb Aharon'le who received a child but lost his life. From these he explains that daily tefillah can only redirect the flow decided on Rosh Hashanah, and that one Rosh Hashanah can decide matters for many years, as with Yosef.

title.en: Why the barren were remembered on Rosh Hashanah itself

summary.en: The Rav asks why Sarah, Rachel and Chana were helped on Rosh Hashanah itself, and explains that theirs was a special, general remembrance that came straight from the day of creation, yesh me'ayin. Rosh Hashanah is therefore the time when every 'barren' person, including one whose tefillah or learning is barren, can be remembered, and the Torah readings of the day are made of these very letters.

title.en: Rosh Hashanah, the Yerushalayim of time

summary.en: Using the Sefer Yetzirah's three dimensions of world, year and soul, the Rav explains that Rosh Hashanah is in time what Yerushalayim is in place: the beginning and the seat of the King, where one bows in self-nullification. On the regalim a Jew must go up to Yerushalayim, but on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur the kingship comes to every Jew, so the whole world becomes Yerushalayim.

title.en: Yerushalayim, the barren one, to be remembered

summary.en: The Rav says Rosh Hashanah is the time to pray for Eretz Yisrael and Yerushalayim, which are 'not worse than Sarah, Rachel and Chana', since from them came Klal Yisrael and Moshiach. He brings the zichronos verse that remembers the land, the field of Efron that 'rose' when it passed to Avraham, the mourning roads of Tzion, and the haftarah blessing and verse that call Tzion a barren woman awaiting her children.

title.en: Every Jew can bring the remembrance

summary.en: The Rav says every Jew must arouse mercy for barren Yerushalayim, the mother of Klal Yisrael, as one would seek every remedy for a barren relative. He tells the Chasam Sofer's story of a woman in hard labor helped when a man who had read the Rosh Hashanah haftarah entered, and the Ba'al Shem Tov's story of a village boy whose whistle annulled a decree, concluding that no one knows whose simple, pure prayer will bring Moshiach.

title.en: The nations convene over Yerushalayim

summary.en: The Rav describes how on Rosh Hashanah the fate of every country is decided, and contrasts this with the newspapers' picture of nations gathering in Washington and at the UN to decide the fate of Yerushalayim and Eretz Yisrael. He sets aside the political question and asks how those who sit there could decide a matter that Hashem, who alone rules Klal Yisrael without any heavenly prince, has not yet decided.

title.en: The earthly uproar reflects heaven

summary.en: The Rav brings the Chafetz Chaim's comment on the Balfour Declaration and explains it: what people stir about on earth is a sign of what is happening in heaven, like a radio set catching waves, as the Midrash learns from what people said about Leah. Yet the geulah itself does not depend on any person, as the Maharal shows from the Torah's not naming Amram and Yocheved, and as the Midrash shows about Titus and the Churban.

title.en: No person destroyed or will rebuild Yerushalayim

summary.en: The Rav brings the Gemara that the humility of Rabbi Zechariah ben Avkulas destroyed the Beis Hamikdash and explains that no person truly destroyed Yerushalayim; Chazal recorded it only to teach a lesson, since good is brought through the worthy. He then brings the Chasam Sofer's allusion in the name Pinchas ben Elazar ben Aharon haKohen that Eliyahu, who brings the union of the holy Names, will announce the rebuilding of Yerushalayim.

title.en: Their stirring must do something in heaven

summary.en: The Rav describes the world seething over Camp David and the votes on Eretz Yisrael, and argues that the nations cannot by their own power open heaven to decide about Yerushalayim. Since they know from the Bible that the land was promised to the Jews and pretend not to know, their uproar is rebellion, and in heaven it produces only a great laugh.

title.en: 'Why do the nations rage': Hashem laughs

summary.en: The Rav reads Tehillim 2: the nations' uproar against Hashem and His anointed is an attempt to throw off the yoke of Heaven, and 'He who sits in heaven laughs' at it; Hashem alone decides who owns Tzion, and in the end the whole world will belong to the Jews. He adds that this is not a statement about the present government, and explains why the Torah reading about Yishmael is read on Rosh Hashanah, contrasting Hagar's tears with Rachel weeping for her children.

title.en: Fear of Heaven with joy

summary.en: The Rav says Rosh Hashanah is the time to draw fear of Heaven for the whole year, a higher fear of the King rather than fear for oneself. He brings the Chasam Sofer's parable on Nechemiah's 'eat rich foods': a servant facing judgment who rejoiced at the king's coronation and was raised up, and says this is the point of the Ba'al Shem Tov's disciples that Rosh Hashanah is a day of joy, possible only for one who prepared with teshuvah.

title.en: Success through being nothing

summary.en: The Rav teaches that since on Rosh Hashanah Hashem creates yesh me'ayin, the whole success of the day is to be nothing; one who considers himself 'something' has no share in it. He brings the Gemara that the bent shofar is better, warns against quarrels over honors in shul, and reads 'from your woodchopper to your water drawer' as everyone, great and small, standing as the smallest.

title.en: Drawing kingship for a new year

summary.en: The Rav reads 'to enter the covenant of Hashem' as the judgment of how much G-dliness a Jew will have all year, citing Likkutei Torah, and says each year brings a new conduct from Above. As the Gemara says, malchiyos make Hashem King, and as one accepts the kingship on Rosh Hashanah so He reigns all year; when one feels nothing on Rosh Hashanah, the Ba'al Shem Tov's counsel is to bind oneself to all the tzaddikim and all of Klal Yisrael.

title.en: Joining all of Klal Yisrael, and the closing prayer

summary.en: The Rav explains 'all of you before Hashem': even a fingernail has a good year when the head and heart feel Rosh Hashanah, and 'teruah' means friendship with all Jews, through which judgment departs. He tells of Reb Zusha and the wagon of hay, explains Mordechai's answer 'I am a Jew', and closes by urging that 'Hamelech' be said with real acceptance of the kingship, praying for the revelation of Hashem's kingship over the world and salvation for all Jews.

catalogTitle: A Deeper Understanding of the עבד עברי: His Slavery and Redemption

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that the Jewish slave sold to an idolatrous temple, called 'eiker' (root) by the Torah, can never be uprooted from his place in the Jewish people, because Hashem protests and promises his redemption, and he links this return to Yovel and to Shavuos.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with a parable: Torah is a field with ever deeper treasures, and the same Chumash and Gemara are learned from childhood to old age and by all the generations back to Moshe Rabbeinu. Turning to the parsha, he outlines Shemitah, Yovel and the Jewish slave, who sold himself after neglecting Shemitah and is degraded so far that he may live with a non-Jewish maidservant. Every Jew is a letter in the Sefer Torah, so slavery is an uprooting. The Torah calls idolatry 'eiker' only where a Jew is sold to it, because there Hashem protests: no Jew may reach the point of no return, and idolatry itself will be uprooted. Following the Baal HaTurim's nineteen redemptions, he matches the verses to blessings of Shemoneh Esrei. Finally he shows that Shavuos, the fiftieth day, is a Yovel of return, as seen in Rus returning to Beis Lechem Yehudah.

en: Torah can be dug deeper and deeper without end, so the same Chumash and Gemara serve a child, an old man and every generation back to Sinai.
A Jew who becomes a slave, through neglecting Shemitah or through theft, is cut off from his roots in the Jewish family, as shown by his permission to live with a non-Jewish maidservant.
Every Jew is a letter in the Sefer Torah, rooted in the Torah, and Yovel restores him to his family, his land and his home.
The word 'eiker' for idolatry is Hashem's protest: when a Jew is sold to idolatry, Hashem will uproot the idolatry rather than let the Jew be uprooted forever.
Shavuos, the fiftieth day after seven weeks, is a Yovel: the day of freedom and return to one's roots.

title.en: The endless depth of Torah

summary.en: The Rav compares Torah to a field with silver, gold and diamonds ever deeper, and contrasts secular textbooks a student outgrows with the Chumash and Gemara a Jew learns his whole life, the same ones used back to Moshe Rabbeinu. He calls this a visible miracle in a time of hester panim and explains that he will try to go below the surface in these weekly sessions.

title.en: Shemitah, Yovel and the Jewish slave

summary.en: The Rav outlines the sedra's laws of Shemitah and Yovel, then the Jewish slave: his comfortable conditions, his permission to live with a non-Jewish maidservant, and his release after six years or, if he chooses to stay, at Yovel.

title.en: How a Jew falls into slavery

summary.en: The Rav brings the Talmud that a man sells himself because he did not keep Shemitah and lost field, house and belongings, or is sold for theft. Slavery degrades him from the holiness of the Jewish people, and Yovel frees him and returns his field so he can start life again.

title.en: Sold to a gentile and to idolatry

summary.en: The Rav reads the verses of a Jew sold to a wealthy gentile and to 'eiker', which the Gemara in Kiddushin explains as idolatry itself. It is a mitzvah for a brother or relative to redeem him before he sinks in, and Hashem explains that the Jews are His servants whom He took out of Mitzrayim.

title.en: Uprooted from his roots, and why 'eiker'

summary.en: The Rav explains that every Jew is a letter in the Sefer Torah, so the slave's permission to marry a non-Jewish maidservant is a violent severance from his roots. He asks why the Torah calls idolatry 'eiker' only here, brings the Gemara that it will be uprooted, and the promise that no one will be cast away from the Jewish people forever.

title.en: No point of no return: Hashem's protest

summary.en: The Rav lays out the levels of descent: slavery, not leaving after six years, being sold to a gentile, and worst of all to idolatry. As in Mitzrayim, where Hashem took the Jews out at the forty-ninth gate of impurity, Hashem tolerates the lower levels but protests the last; 'eiker' is that protest, a promise that the Jew will be brought back.

title.en: Nineteen redemptions and Shemoneh Esrei

summary.en: The Rav brings the Baal HaTurim that the root 'geulah' appears nineteen times in the sedra, matching the nineteen blessings of Shemoneh Esrei, and matches the redemption from 'eiker' to Velamalshinim, 'one of his brothers shall redeem him' to Al HaTzaddikim, and 'dodo' to David, Mashiach ben David: a promise for the individual and for the whole people.

title.en: Shavuos is Yovel

summary.en: The Rav parallels the seven Shemitos and Yovel with the seven weeks and Shavuos, when heaven came down to earth. Shabbos means return, yet many do not use it; on Shavuos heaven comes down to bring a person back, freedom as in 'charus-cheirus', and Hashem chooses to uproot idolatry rather than the Jew.

title.en: Rus returns to Beis Lechem Yehudah

summary.en: The Rav explains that a convert's soul must return to its roots, as Rus returned from the field of Moav to Beis Lechem Yehudah, whose initials spell Yovel. Eretz Yisrael is like a Sefer Torah, Rachel was promised there that her children will return, and he describes Shavuos as the day to leave the 'spiritual intermarriage' with gentile culture.

title.en: Questions; Yovel as shofar and stream

summary.en: The Rav answers listeners' questions: about a woman who married a gentile he says both answers are true, she will be punished but eventually return; he explains why he said 'faces in heaven'. He adds that Yovel means both shofar and stream, linking it to the haftarah's tree planted by water, and closes with a remark on Yerushalayim.

catalogTitle: ר"ה שחל בשבת - השבת ממתקת הדינים; צריכים להיות בידידות עם השבת

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that when Rosh Hashanah falls on Shabbos, Shabbos itself takes the place of the shofar and sweetens the judgment, so a Jew must make Shabbos his close friend, above all in this year of Shabbos and shemittah.

abstract.en: On the twenty-fifth of Elul the Rav opens with the shofar's power to bring a Jew's remembrance 'inside', to the place of Divine will. He brings a question from a sefer heard as 'Avi Nachal': if the passuk in Emor speaks of Rosh Hashanah on Shabbos, why must it forbid melachah? The answer comes through a mashal of a merchant whose advocate is absent and whose relative must defend him: the shofar is the advocate, Shabbos is the relative, and the Torah advises reconciling with Shabbos by keeping it properly. He then shows that this year is full of Shabbos: Rosh Hashanah, Shemini Atzeres, both ends of Chanukah and Tu BiShvat fall on Shabbos, in a shemittah year. Through Rashi, the Ramban, shemittah and yovel, he explains that refraining from blowing for Shabbos's sake, joined with the pesukim, reaches the level of yovel. He describes true Shabbos observance, above all in speech, explains the Rosh Hashanah readings about barren women as a prayer for Yerushalayim, and closes with the Chasam Sofer on joy on Rosh Hashanah.

en: When Rosh Hashanah falls on Shabbos and the shofar cannot be blown, Shabbos itself stands up for the Jew in judgment, more than the shofar would.
The passuk's 'you shall do no melachah' is advice to reconcile with Shabbos by taking on to keep it properly, since one who has slighted Shabbos cannot expect it to defend him.
This year Rosh Hashanah, Shemini Atzeres, the first and last days of Chanukah and Tu BiShvat all fall on Shabbos, and it is a shemittah year, so the whole year calls for a close bond with Shabbos.
Refraining from the shofar for the sake of Shabbos is itself a merit of Shabbos observance, and together with the pesukim of zichronos and shofaros it reaches as high as the shofar.
True Shabbos is not only putting down one's tools; for a refined Jew its essence is in speech and thought, speaking only words of Torah.
The Rosh Hashanah readings speak only of barren women being remembered, because the great barren one awaiting remembrance is Yerushalayim.

title.en: The shofar goes inside, and a question on the passuk

summary.en: The Rav notes that the twenty-fifth of Elul is the day creation began, and explains that the shofar, being for remembrance, counts as 'inside' and brings a Jew to the place of Divine will. He then brings the question of a sefer heard as 'Avi Nachal': why does the passuk about Rosh Hashanah on Shabbos need to forbid melachah?

title.en: The mashal of the merchant and his relative

summary.en: The Rav retells the sefer's mashal of a king, a merchant who fell short, an advocate who always defended him, and a relative who defended him in the advocate's absence until the merchant insulted him. The shofar is the advocate, Shabbos is the relative, and one who has slighted Shabbos must first make peace with it.

title.en: Zichron teruah and the advice to keep Shabbos

summary.en: The Rav reads the passuk with the mashal: 'zichron teruah' means only reciting the pesukim, and 'you shall do no melachah' is Hashem's advice to take on keeping Shabbos properly. He stresses that real Shabbos is not just resting from work but holiness, and that such a Shabbos blows the shofar for us.

title.en: The judgment from Rosh Hashanah to Shemini Atzeres

summary.en: The Rav explains that the judgment begins on Rosh Hashanah and is completed only on Shemini Atzeres, when the blessings of rain come down. Hashem gives counsel to turn the judgment to mercy: the shofar, the pesukim of malchiyos, zichronos and shofaros, and the growing mercy of the days that follow.

title.en: A year full of Shabbos

summary.en: The Rav lists the decisive days of this year that fall on Shabbos: Rosh Hashanah, Shemini Atzeres, the first and last days of Chanukah, Rosh Chodesh Shevat and Tu BiShvat. It is also a shemittah year, a whole year of Shabbos, so one must make Shabbos a close friend and guard it with a great reckoning.

title.en: The Gemara, Rashi and the Ramban on zichron teruah

summary.en: The Rav brings the Mishnah and the Gemara's derivation of not blowing on Shabbos from the two pesukim, Rava's question from the Mikdash, Rashi in Behar and the Ramban's challenge, and the Chasam Sofer's path. He then brings the Tur Bareket that merely mentioning the shofar helps, supported by the Gemara's mention of Chevron to recall the Avos.

title.en: Shemittah, yovel and the shofar

summary.en: The Rav explains that Shabbos and shemittah carry a power of release from debts, and a Jew's greatest debts are his sins. Yovel, the Shabbos of Shabbosos, is greater still, and the shofar is called yovel; therefore the tekios on Rosh Hashanah carry an aspect of Yom Kippur, and one may confess between them though sin is otherwise not mentioned on Rosh Hashanah.

title.en: Standing on the table of Shabbos

summary.en: The Rav explains with a mashal of a man who stands on a table to reach the ceiling: the pesukim alone or Shabbos alone are not enough, but together they reach the level of yovel. The Torah foresaw the decree not to blow on Shabbos, and the refraining for Shabbos's sake is itself the merit; in the Mikdash there was no decree, so there they blew. He compares it to the Gemara that Shabbos itself brings healing.

title.en: Shabbos sweetens the judgment of creation

summary.en: The Rav explains why the shofar is needed: Rosh Hashanah is the day of creation, which Hashem first intended with strict judgment, as Rashi says, and every year the world is created anew with judgment. The shofar sweetens it, but on Shabbos, Shabbos itself sweetens all judgments, so one must befriend Shabbos, especially in this rare year.

title.en: What true Shabbos observance demands

summary.en: The Rav explains that keeping Shabbos is not only putting down the pen, the hoe and the telephone; since Hashem created the world with speech and ceased from it, the heart of Shabbos for a refined Jew is speech and even thought. He brings the passuk in Yeshayahu, condemns talking business during the Torah reading, and with the Shelah says one must give Shabbos its delight.

title.en: The readings of barren women and Yerushalayim

summary.en: The Rav explains that this year, with no shofar, only the Torah reading remains: Sarah being remembered and Chana in the haftorah. Rosh Hashanah is a time of remembrance for the barren, since Adam was blessed with 'be fruitful' on that day; the readings mention neither judgment nor creation because the great barren one is Yerushalayim, for whose rebuilding and for Moshiach the Musaf prayer asks.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer's mashal of the coronation day

summary.en: The Rav brings Nechemiah's words to the people weeping on Rosh Hashanah, that the joy of Hashem is their strength, and the Chasam Sofer's explanation. Rosh Hashanah is a day of joy in Hashem's kingship, as among the disciples of the Ba'al Shem Tov; in the mashal, a prisoner awaiting judgment on the king's coronation day sings and dances out of love for the king.

title.en: Joy in the King, and closing blessings

summary.en: The Rav finishes the mashal: the king frees the prisoner who could forget his own judgment for the king's joy, and so Nechemiah told the people that rejoicing in Hashem's kingship brings a good verdict. He closes with wishes that Shabbos defend us this year, that we take on Shabbos properly, and for the redemption.

catalogTitle: ר"ה שחל בשבת - "זיך איבערבעטן מיטן שבת"

oneLiner.en: Following the Arvei Nachal, the Rav explains that when Rosh Hashana falls on Shabbos and the shofar is not blown, Shabbos itself pleads for the Jews, so they must make peace with Shabbos by keeping it on the level expected of them.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the Gemara's two pesukim, zichron teruah and yom teruah, and the Arvei Nachal's question: if zichron teruah speaks of Rosh Hashana on Shabbos, why must the Torah add that all labor is forbidden? He retells the Arvei Nachal's parable of a king, a beloved friend's son, his enemy, a lawyer and a powerful relative. In the nimshal the Satan accuses, the shofar is the lawyer, and Shabbos is the relative whom the Jews have offended; the Torah's advice is to appease Shabbos by refraining from melacha. The Rav then shows that melacha is measured by each person's level, so for a ben Torah keeping Shabbos includes speech and thought. He adds that the final sealing reaches Chanukah, which this year ends on Shabbos, speaks of a hoped-for year of redemption, explains the Jews' partnership in creation through malchiyos said with joy, and closes with the Chasam Sofer's teaching that joy in Hashem's kingship is the strength in judgment.

en: The Arvei Nachal asks why the Torah adds that all labor is forbidden if zichron teruah already speaks of Rosh Hashana that falls on Shabbos.
In the parable's nimshal the Satan is the accuser, the shofar is the lawyer who confounds him, and Shabbos is the powerful relative who can plead for the Jews when there is no shofar.
Since many have offended Shabbos, the Torah's advice of refraining from all melacha is the way to appease it, and then Shabbos does even more than the shofar.
What counts as melacha depends on each person's level, so for a talmid chacham Shabbos also means guarding his speech and thought.
Jews become partners in creation on Rosh Hashana, and the pesukim of malchiyos said with joy and acceptance of Hashem's kingship create a world of good.
Following the Chasam Sofer, joy in Hashem's kingship on Rosh Hashana is itself the strength by which one merits in judgment.

candidateTopics: Rosh Hashana that falls on Shabbos
joy in Hashem's kingship on Rosh Hashana

title.en: The Arvei Nachal's question on zichron teruah

summary.en: The Rav introduces the Arvei Nachal and the Gemara's two pesukim, zichron teruah and yom teruah, with Rashi's and the Ramban's views. He brings the Arvei Nachal's question why the passuk adds that all labor is forbidden if it already speaks of Shabbos.

title.en: Parable of the king and his friend's son

summary.en: The Rav retells, briefly, the Arvei Nachal's parable: a king's beloved supplier dies, his son inherits the concession, an enemy at court keeps accusing him, and a skilled lawyer or a powerful relative defends him. When the lawyer is away and the son has quarreled with the relative, the king sends him advice to make peace with the relative.

title.en: Shabbos, the relative who pleads for Israel

summary.en: The Rav explains the nimshal: the Avos are the beloved friends, the Satan accuses on Rosh Hashana, the shofar is the lawyer, and Shabbos, a day of the neshamah, is the relative. Because Jews have slighted Shabbos, the Torah advises them through 'all labor you shall not do' to appease it, and then Shabbos pleads for them even more than the shofar.

title.en: Each person judged by his level

summary.en: The Rav explains that melacha is defined by each person's level and shows that Chazal judge greater people more strictly: the Gemara on arrogance, the poskim on walking without netilas yadayim, and parables of a stain on a potato sack versus a silk shirt and ten hours of learning for a bochur versus a gadol.

title.en: Shabbos in speech and thought

summary.en: The Rav contrasts a simple farmer's Shabbos with that of a talmid chacham: since Hashem created the world with speech and thought, a ben Torah must rest from mundane speech and thought too. Citing the Shelah, he says Shabbos must have pleasure from the person, through Torah, davening, zemiros and holy talk, and that on this Rosh Hashana one must make peace with Shabbos.

title.en: Sealing until Chanukah, and Tu BiShvat on Shabbos

summary.en: The Rav describes how the sealing of judgment extends from Yom Kippur to Shemini Atzeres and, according to students of the Ba'al Shem Tov, to the last day of Chanukah, which this year falls on Shabbos, as does the Rosh Hashana for trees. He urges a reckoning after every Shabbos whether it brought Hashem nachas.

title.en: Shabbos on the fish; a year of redemption

summary.en: The Rav tells of a poor chassid who prayed over his challah and fish that Hashem give him Shabbos on them, and explains that one eats Shabbos food in honor of Shabbos. He then mentions a calculation attributed to the Vilna Gaon pointing to the coming year as a time of redemption, and asks that it be a year of favor.

title.en: Partners in creation through malchiyos

summary.en: The Rav explains that on Rosh Hashana the world is created anew, and Jews become Hashem's partners, especially on Shabbos through saying Vayechulu. The ten pesukim of each blessing parallel the ten utterances of creation, so saying them with joy and acceptance of Hashem's kingship creates a world of blessing, and each verse said is like one of those utterances.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer: joy in the King's coronation

summary.en: The Rav brings the Chasam Sofer on Nechemia's words to eat and rejoice on Rosh Hashana, with the parable of an imprisoned servant who dances on the king's coronation day and is freed for it. He concludes that rejoicing in Hashem's kingship, the true oneg of Shabbos on such a Rosh Hashana, is the strength in judgment, and ends with blessings for the new year.

catalogTitle: דרוש נפלא בענין התענוג הגדול של יראת שמים (שייכות לפרשת נצבים)

oneLiner.en: Through the mitzvah of hakhel and the order of Maseches Rosh Hashanah, the Rav explains that Rosh Hashanah is the 'king' of the year, and that the fear of the King it brings is, for a Jew, a sweet fear mixed with joy, a foretaste of Moshiach.

abstract.en: The Rav opens by asking why the Mishnah in Rosh Hashanah begins the laws of shofar only after the story of Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua. He turns to hakhel in the week's parsha: why the little children were brought, Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah's derashah, and the Chasam Sofer's explanation. A king, he explains, is the garment of Heaven's kingship and the channel of all blessing, and one must fear him; leaders may be chosen by Heaven or by the people. Rosh Hashanah is the king and the 'nasi' of the year, which is why the nasi fixes its date and the shofar chapter follows. Hakhel gathers all souls as Rosh Hashanah gathers all days; the shofar speaks beyond words. The fear Rosh Hashanah brings is a sweet fear, a taste of Moshiach. Reconciling the Chasam Sofer's joy with the Arizal's tears, he describes weeping of joy at returning to the Father, using Hoshea and Yirmiyahu, and closes with preparing in Elul and on the last Shabbos.

en: The king is the garment and representative of Heaven's kingship in this world, and the channel through which all blessing reaches the people; therefore the Torah commands fear of the king.
Rosh Hashanah is the 'king' and head of the whole year, containing all its days, just as the king contains the whole people; from it one can draw fear of Heaven for the entire year.
Hakhel gathers all Jewish souls to the king, as Rosh Hashanah gathers all the days of the year; the shofar, like the king's reading, speaks to the soul in a voice above words.
The fear of Hashem a Jew asks for on Rosh Hashanah is a sweet fear, a fear of His greatness and goodness that is itself a pleasure, a foretaste of the fear Moshiach's shofar will bring.
The tears of Rosh Hashanah should be tears of joy mixed with shame, of a child returning to his Father, as the Chasam Sofer reads 'bechiyah' in the verse 'b'shimcha yegilun kol hayom'.
Such tears of returning cannot come suddenly; one must prepare for them through the teshuvah of Elul and Selichos.

candidateTopics: Rosh Hashanah as king of the year
weeping of joy on Rosh Hashanah

title.en: Why a new chapter for shofar?

summary.en: The Rav notes the precision in Rebbi's arrangement of the Mishnah and asks why, after two chapters on sanctifying the month and a short Mishnah on the same topic, a new chapter on the shofar begins. He then introduces the week's parsha: Moshe writes the whole Torah and commands the mitzvah of hakhel.

title.en: Hakhel and the little children

summary.en: The Rav describes hakhel after a year of avodah and asks why little children who understand nothing were brought. He brings Rabbi Yehoshua's mother bringing his cradle to the beis medrash, Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah's derashah in Chagigah, and the Chasam Sofer: parents give up their own spiritual gain for their children, like Avraham who chose to teach others over Chanoch's solitary holiness.

title.en: What a king is: the channel of blessing

summary.en: The Rav explains that the king contains the whole people and is the garment of Heaven's kingship, the 'parnas' through whom all influence flows; Pharaoh rejected interpretations of his Rosh Hashanah dreams that did not concern the people's livelihood, and talmidei chachamim are likewise called kings. He distinguishes a leader chosen for his own merits, like Yosef, from one appointed by the people for the sake of Heaven.

title.en: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua

summary.en: The Rav retells the end of the second chapter of Rosh Hashanah: Rabban Gamliel ordered Rabbi Yehoshua to come with his staff and money on the day that was Yom Kippur by his reckoning; Rabbi Yehoshua came, and Rabban Gamliel kissed him on the head. The Gemara teaches that even a lesser leader, once appointed, is like the greatest, and one may not say the earlier days were better.

title.en: Fear of the king; Rosh Hashanah as king

summary.en: The Rav asks why one must fear the king and answers that he is the garment of Heaven's kingship, so fearing him leads to fear of Heaven. Applying the Sefer Yetzirah's world, year and soul, he explains that Rosh Hashanah is the king and 'nasi' of the year, from which fear of Heaven is drawn for the whole year; therefore the nasi fixes Rosh Hashanah, and Rabbi Yehoshua submitted.

title.en: Two kinds of Rosh Hashanah, two kinds of leader

summary.en: The Rav explains that Rosh Hashanah can be fixed by beis din or, when beis din did not sanctify the month, by Heaven; likewise a leader may be appointed by the people or by Heaven. The help from Above is the same, but the 'taste' differs, and on Rosh Hashanah Jews ask for a revealed kingship, 'Hashem ori', a shining face and not a hidden one. This is why the shofar chapter follows the story: it is the introduction to accepting the King.

title.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah, chosen by Heaven

summary.en: The Rav explains that Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah was a nasi chosen by Heaven, shown by the miracle of his white beard at eighteen. Since every tzaddik darshens according to the root of his soul, he darshened hakhel as a Father turning His face to His children: the generation is not orphaned. Hakhel gathers all souls to the king, as Rosh Hashanah gathers all days.

title.en: Gathering on Rosh Hashanah; the voice of the shofar

summary.en: The Rav brings Rabbi Aharon of Karlin on coming to the Rebbe for Rosh Hashanah, since a gathering reveals more of Heaven's kingship. Each soul is a letter of the Torah; once Moshe completed the Torah, hakhel followed, and the king reads its letters to the gathered souls. The shofar speaks in a voice above words that the soul hears, as the children at hakhel absorb what they cannot understand.

title.en: The King of kings and the fear of Moshiach's shofar

summary.en: The Rav describes the ascending kings: the king of each generation, the soul of Adam revealed in David and in Moshiach, and Hashem Himself on the Rosh Hashanah of the future. When Moshiach's great shofar sounds, the nations will hide from the fear of Hashem's greatness, not from punishment. Every Jewish king and every Rosh Hashanah is a taste of this, and a tzaddik's description of Moshiach comforting each Jew is brought.

title.en: The sweet fear only a Jew can taste

summary.en: With the Bnei Yissaschar on 'ki ein machsor lirei'av', the Rav explains that a Jew's fear of Hashem is not a lack but a pleasure: the soul has strings tuned to Moshiach that the shofar plays. He ties it to 'lefanav naavod b'yirah vafachad' on Friday night and 'uvchen ten pachdecha' on Rosh Hashanah, and explains that one fears Rosh Hashanah itself, a king with a crown, because Heaven's kingship is revealed in it.

title.en: Adam, David, Moshiach and the tekios

summary.en: The Rav explains that Rosh Hashanah is the day Adam was created, whose soul is that of David and Moshiach; Jews' teshuvah repairs Adam's sin and prepares for Moshiach. Following the kavanos in the siddur of Rabbi Yaakov Emden, the tekios draw down the Avos with David, and the tekiah gedolah is the shofar of Moshiach that gathers all souls, the great hakhel.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer: rejoicing on the day of judgment

summary.en: The Rav brings the Chasam Sofer on Nechemiah's 'al te'atzvu', which seems to contradict the trembling of the mussar sefarim. The Chasam Sofer's mashal: a prisoner danced on the king's coronation day, the day of his own trial, and the king freed him for forgetting himself in the king's joy. One who rejoices that Hashem has become King is strengthened in judgment.

title.en: Weeping of joy: the Arizal and the Chasam Sofer

summary.en: The Rav brings the Arizal that one who does not weep on Rosh Hashanah lacks wholeness of soul, and the Chasam Sofer that 'b'shimcha yegilun kol hayom' forms the acronym 'bechiyah', weeping of joy. Weeping is strong emotion, as Rabbi Akiva wept on Shabbos at Shir Hashirim; on Rosh Hashanah it is the bittersweet weeping of a child returning to his Father, which leads to Hoshea, the prophet of teshuvah.

title.en: Hoshea: a child cannot be exchanged

summary.en: The Rav reads the opening of Hoshea with Rashi: Hashem tells the prophet to take a wife of harlotry and, when he cannot exchange his own children, teaches that Hashem will not exchange His. The children's names Lo-ruchama and Lo-ammi are reversed, Hashem loves Israel even in their lowly state, and in the end they will return and 'fear Hashem and His goodness', a fear of goodness that is pure sweetness.

title.en: Preparing in Elul and on the last Shabbos

summary.en: From the second-day haftarah, 'bivchi yavo'u', the Rav explains that Jews will weep because they return to their Father, and every Rosh Hashanah is a taste of this. Such tears need preparation through Elul and Selichos; without it one must start from the simple shofar of awakening. He closes on the last Shabbos of Elul, which must be prepared for with longing, bringing Rabbi Shlomo of Karlin on one who keeps Shabbos without desire.

catalogTitle: יובל - Returning to the Roots

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that Yovel, like Shavuos, means a return to the roots, so that even a Jew sold to serve an idol, and a Jewish soul like Rus born among the nations, is brought back to Hashem.

abstract.en: The Rav opens by comparing Yovel to Shavuos: after seven cycles of seven comes the fiftieth, the start of an eighth week above nature, and Yovel means returning to the roots. He turns to the Jew in Behar who was sold to serve an idol, a fall that came from trading in Shemitah produce, and asks why only here the Torah calls idolatry 'eiker', something to be uprooted. His answer: when Hashem sees His child swallowed by avodah zarah, He declares that it will be uprooted and that the Jew must be redeemed. He brings the Ba'al HaTurim that the parsha holds nineteen forms of 'geulah' matching the nineteen brachos of Shemoneh Esrei. He then shows how Rus, a Jewish soul hidden among the nations, came back to Beis Lechem, the place of Yovel, of Malchus Beis David and of Rachel's grave, and closes with Shavuos as a reunion of chassan and kallah.

en: Shavuos, the fiftieth day and the start of the eighth week above nature, is the Yovel of the year, and Yovel means returning to the roots.
The Jew sold to serve an idol fell so low because he violated the kedushah of Shemitah, and therefore Shemitah could not free him; only Yovel brings him out.
Only here does the Torah call idolatry 'eiker', because when a Jew is swallowed by it Hashem declares that it will be uprooted and His child redeemed.
Following the Ba'al HaTurim, the parsha with its nineteen forms of 'geulah' is itself a Shemoneh Esrei, a tefillah for the redemption of Klal Yisrael.
Rus was a Jewish soul hidden among the nations, and she returned specifically to Beis Lechem, the place of Yovel and of Malchus Beis David.
Shavuos is a teshuvah of return and a wedding: Hashem and Klal Yisrael, once united, come back together.
